opener: TOLLPASS NOTICE: You have an unpaid toll of $6.80 from 10/14. Failure to pay within 48 hours results in a $75 late fee. Pay now: {{PRACTICE_LINK}}

stages.name: hook
stages.llmGuidance: You're a TollPass automated system. Cite a specific small toll amount and a large penalty. Keep it terse and official.
stages.scriptedFallback: Reminder: $6.80 toll balance due. $75 penalty applies after 48 hours. Use the link above.

stages.name: engage
stages.llmGuidance: User replied. Confirm their license plate is on file (use a generic format like 'plate ending in ***4B') and urge them to verify payment.
stages.scriptedFallback: Our records show plate ending ***4B with an outstanding balance. Please verify at the link to avoid DMV reporting.

stages.name: escalate
stages.llmGuidance: Mention that unpaid tolls may be reported to the DMV and affect vehicle registration renewal. Time is running out.
stages.scriptedFallback: ⚠️ Unpaid tolls are now subject to DMV reporting. This can delay your registration renewal. Act before midnight: {{PRACTICE_LINK}}

stages.name: ask
stages.llmGuidance: Direct them to the link to pay the $6.80 with a card. Mention they can also dispute the toll at the same link.
stages.scriptedFallback: Pay $6.80 or file a dispute at: {{PRACTICE_LINK}} — card payment only, no cash or check.

stages.name: reveal
stages.scriptedFallback: 🛑 PRACTICE SCAM — This was a Safe Signal exercise. TollPass sends official notices by mail, not SMS payment links.

hook.explanation: 48-hour window with a $75 penalty is designed to panic you
Official toll agencies send mail, not SMS payment links
Collecting payments via SMS link is not how government toll systems work

engage.explanation: Using a partial plate number (easy to guess) creates false sense of legitimacy

escalate.explanation: Invoking DMV and registration is a scare tactic to force quick action

ask.explanation: Real toll agencies offer multiple payment methods including check and app
